title: Upstream-deleted WhatsApp message stays in turns, so its pending candidate stays reviewable and its approved claim stays trusted after removal
repro: Ingest 2 messages, approve both candidates (2 verified claims), drop message m1 from the fetcher, re-ingest: claims=2, turns=2. Base ingest only upserts turns, never removes; checkEvidence still matches the stale stored turn. ingest.ts comment says 'Edited/removed source turns must lose trust' but only edits are handled.
fix_direction: Re-ingest should tombstone/remove turns absent from the fetched snapshot (or invalidate candidates whose turn id is absent from the snapshot) in the same transaction as the claim revocation; add a regression test using the repro above. Must land before mount.

title: Invalidation is not atomic with the raw turn upsert: if invalidateStaleWhatsAppCandidates fails after base.ingestGroup replaced turns, the approved claim keeps the old quote until a later successful ingest
repro: Approve candidate on 'Scholarship closes Friday.'; edit source to Sunday; make invalidate throw (db blip) after base ingest: claims table still holds the Friday claim (probe printed stale claim text still trusted = true). The quarantine audit does not check claim evidence against current turn text, so nothing reports it.
fix_direction: Run invalidation first against the fetched snapshot, or have the audit also flag claims whose evidence quote no longer equals the turn text.

title: Mutation survivors: materialiser claim status 'verified', excluded/non-approved guards in materialiser, and the three tenant scopes in invalidate/revoke are unasserted
repro: Throwaway-copy mutants: status 'verified'->'needs-review' (SURVIVED, no test asserts the status), personal-excluded guard removed (SURVIVED), non-approved guard removed (SURVIVED), invalidate row.tenantId guard removed (SURVIVED), invalidate find unscoped (SURVIVED), revokeWhatsAppClaim deleteOne unscoped (SURVIVED). The two guards are redundant defence in depth with decide(), but no test calls materializeWhatsAppClaim directly.
fix_direction: Direct materialiser unit test (status, refusals) and a cross-tenant invalidate test with both tenants holding claims.

title: Edit-then-revert leaves an approved candidate with no claim and no way to re-materialise (re-approve returns ok changed:false); admitted gap 5 confirmed
repro: Approve, edit source (claim revoked), revert source, re-ingest: pending re-proposal absent (same id exists as approved), approved rows=2 vs claims=1.
fix_direction: Re-materialise on re-ingest when an approved row's evidence matches again, or mark revoked state in the row (needs schema enum change).

title: POLICY FOR UMESH: approved WhatsApp chat statement becomes claims.status 'verified'; elsewhere 'verified' means hand-verified claim and feeds analytics verified ratio
repro: analyticsModel.ts counts status==='verified'; indexing/session.ts comment treats non-needs-review as hand-verified; materializer.ts sets verified for any approved chat message regardless of sender trust. Sensible only if approval means 'publishable and source-grounded', not 'factually verified'.
fix_direction: Umesh decides: keep verified, or add a distinct review-approved marker/status via schema change. No mount until decided.

title: Read-side quarantine not enforced: raw WhatsApp turns and any pre-existing WhatsApp claims/chunks are served by trusted readers
repro: Non-test readers with no WhatsApp predicate: apps/api/src/ask/ask-arms.ts (lexical turns, tree and vector arms), ask/source-context.ts, search-store.ts, semantic-search/semantic-search-store.ts, grounded-content/reader.ts, store.ts (sessions/turns/claims detail), claims/router.ts via store, transcript-review/planner.ts, packages/index/src/graph/build-graph.ts and routes/graph, packages/ask. Pre-existing on main (old wiring indexes WhatsApp with needs-review claims); not a regression of this lane, which is unmounted.
fix_direction: Follow-up unit: shared predicate excluding sessions whose source.kind is whatsapp-batch unless the row is an approved candidate's own claim, applied to each reader above with planted-text tests per criterion 9; plus purge/audit of already-indexed WhatsApp rows.

repro: indexing/session.ts:164 deleteMany by evidence.sessionId; whatsapp/store.ts:168 session replaceOne with index pending. No current caller indexes WhatsApp sessions in the lane; relevant only if a batch indexer or backfill is pointed at them.
